claim: The HIVE study enrolled 213-340 households of 3 or more individuals in Southeastern Michigan each year.
source: These households are followed prospectively from October to April, with symptom-triggered collection of nasal and throat swab specimens for identification of respiratory viruses by RT-PCR (see Materials and methods).
evidence: The manuscript directly states the number of households enrolled and their composition.

claim: In the HIVE study, respiratory specimens were collected 0-7 days after illness onset in the first four seasons (2010-2011 through 2013-2014).
source: In the first four seasons of the study (2010–2011 through 2013–2014), respiratory specimens were collected 0–7 days after illness onset.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the specimen collection timing for the first four seasons.

claim: Beginning in the 2014-2015 season, each individual provided two samples: a self-collected specimen at symptom onset and a clinic-collected specimen obtained 0-7 days later.
source: Beginning in the 2014–2015 season, each individual provided two samples, a self-collected specimen at the time of symptom onset and a clinic-collected specimen obtained 0–7 days later.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the change in sampling protocol for the 2014-2015 season.

claim: Each year, 59-69% of individuals had self-reported or confirmed receipt of that season's vaccine prior to local circulation of influenza virus.
source: Each year, 59–69% of individuals had self-reported or confirmed receipt of that season's vaccine prior to local circulation of influenza virus.
evidence: The manuscript provides specific vaccination rates for the cohort.

claim: Over five seasons and nearly 6290 person-seasons of observation, 77 cases of influenza A/H1N1pdm09 infection and 313 cases of influenza A/H3N2 infection were identified.
source: Over five seasons and nearly 6290 person-seasons of observation, we identified 77 cases of influenza A/H1N1pdm09 infection and 313 cases of influenza A/H3N2 infection (Table 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the number of infections identified over the study period.

claim: Approximately half of the cases (n = 166) were identified in the 2014-2015 season, in which there was an antigenic mismatch between the vaccine and circulating strains.
source: Approximately half of the cases (n = 166) were identified in the 2014–2015 season, in which there was an antigenic mismatch between the vaccine and circulating strains (Flannery et al., 2016).
evidence: The manuscript states the number of cases in 2014-2015 and cites a reference for the antigenic mismatch.

claim: All seasons except 2014-2015 were antigenically matched between vaccine and circulating strains.
source: All other seasons were antigenically matched.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states that other seasons were antigenically matched.

claim: 249 high quality specimens from 200 individuals were analyzed, which had a viral load of >10³ copies per microliter of transport media, adequate RT-PCR amplification of all eight genomic segments, and an average read coverage of >10³ across the genome.
source: Accordingly, we report data on 249 high quality specimens from 200 individuals, which had a viral load of >103 copies per microliter of transport media, adequate RT-PCR amplification of all eight genomic segments, and an average read coverage of >103 across the genome (Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly describes the quality criteria for specimens included in the analysis.

claim: 243 out of 249 samples had fewer than 10 minority iSNV (median 2, IQR 1-3).
source: Two hundred forty-three out of the 249 samples had fewer than 10 minority iSNV (median 2, IQR 1–3).
evidence: The manuscript provides specific statistics on the number of minority iSNV per sample.

claim: Six samples had greater than 10 minority iSNV.
source: There were six samples with greater than 10 minority iSNV.
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the number of samples with more than 10 minority iSNV.

claim: In 3 of the 6 cases with greater than 10 minority iSNV, the frequency distribution of minority iSNVs was bimodal, suggesting that the iSNV were linked and that the samples represented mixed infections.
source: In 3 of these cases, the frequency distribution of minority iSNVs was bimodal, suggesting that the iSNV were linked and that the samples represented mixed infections.
evidence: The manuscript describes the frequency distribution pattern and interprets it as evidence of mixed infections.

claim: Putative genomic haplotypes based on minority iSNV in suspected mixed infections clustered with distinct isolates on phylogenetic trees.
source: Consistent with this hypothesis, putative genomic haplotypes based on these minority iSNV clustered with distinct isolates on phylogenetic trees (Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3), and these samples were removed from subsequent analysis.

claim: The number of minority iSNV identified was not affected by the day of infection, viral load, subtype, or vaccination status.
source: While viral shedding was well correlated with days post symptom onset (Figure 1A), the number of minority iSNV identified was not affected by the day of infection, viral load, subtype, or vaccination status (Figure 1B and C, and Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The manuscript states the lack of correlation and references supporting figures.

claim: Single nucleotide variants were distributed evenly across the genome.
source: Single nucleotide variants were distributed evenly across the genome (Figure 1D).
evidence: The manuscript states the distribution pattern and references a supporting figure.

claim: 98% of minority iSNV were only found once, 2.3% were found in two individuals, and no minority iSNV were found in three or more individuals.
source: Ninety-eight percent of minority iSNV were only found once, 2.3% were found in two individuals, and no minority iSNV were found in three or more individuals.

source: The low level of shared diversity suggests that within-host populations explore distinct regions of sequence space with little evidence for parallel evolution.

claim: Of the 12 minority iSNV that were found in multiple individuals, three were nonsynonymous and none were present in antigenic epitopes.

claim: The ratio of nonsynonymous to synonymous variants was 0.75.

claim: The data suggest significant purifying selection within hosts.

claim: It is estimated that 131 of the 329 amino acids in HA1 lie in or near antigenic sites.

claim: 16 minority nonsynonymous iSNV were identified in antigenic regions.

claim: Mutations in antigenic epitopes were not present at significantly higher within-host frequencies than other nonsynonymous mutations in HA.
source: Although we identified 16 minority nonsynonymous iSNV in these regions (Supplementary file 2), mutations in antigenic epitopes were not present at significantly higher within-host frequencies than other nonsynonymous mutations in HA (Figure 2B).
evidence: The manuscript states the lack of significant difference and references a supporting figure.

claim: Five putative antigenic variants were in positions that have been experimentally shown to differ among antigenically drifted viruses.
source: Five putative antigenic variants were in positions that have been experimentally shown to differ among antigenically drifted viruses (Smith et al., 2004; Wiley et al., 1981), and two (193S and 189N) lie in the 'antigenic ridge' that is a major contributor to antigenic drift (Koel et al., 2013).
